abstract: This paper presents an online real-time intelligent system for a heating plant operation support. The intelligent system is established based on INTEMOR software platform, which combines artificial intelligence (AI), computer technology and information technology, and runs in a real-time distributed environment. Many function modules are developed to perform some specific operation support tasks in the heating plant, which include the communication gateway, data processing and analysis, online process monitoring and diagnosis, online operation manual, reasoning system, knowledge base creator and multimedia interface. The structure and the main features of the system are discussed.

articleTitle: Multivariable intelligent decoupling control and its applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Many complex industrial processes are multivariable, strongly coupled, nonlinear and time-variant, and conventional decoupling based control techniques will not work. This paper discusses multivariable intelligent decoupling control algorithms, and develops the three-level multivariable intelligent decoupling technique which can be easily realized in distributed control systems. Finally, examples of successful applications of the multivariable intelligent decoupling control technique in complex industrial processes are given.

articleTitle: Design of fault-tolerant controller for uncertain continuous-time system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on Lyapunov stability theorem and the generalised inverse theory, we present a design procedure for synthesizing a state-feedback system possessing good characteristics due to both the placements of the closed-loop poles in a specified region and the integrity against actuator failures in this paper. Design method for state feedback controller such that all poles of the nominal closed-loop systems are placed within a prescribed circular region is addressed. The region that we consider for pole placement is a specified circular region. Then, the design of robust controller for the system subjected to plant parameter perturbation and actuator failure has been studied. Sufficient condition for the existence of the desired controller is derived. Furthermore, the result is developed for the case of sensor failure. It is shown that the proposed system design retains asymptotic stability in the presence of parameter perturbation, as well as in the case of actuator failure.

articleTitle: The intelligent optimal sieving method for control of FACTS devices in multi-machine systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-target oriented optimal control strategy for FACTS devices installed in multi-machine power systems, named the intelligent optimal sieving control (IOSC) method. This novel method divides the FACTS device output region into several parts and selects one typical value to form each part, which is called output candidate. Then, an intelligent optimal sieve is constructed, which predicts the impacts of each output candidate on a power system and selects an optimal output from all candidates. The artificial neural network technologies and fuzzy methods are applied to build the intelligent sieve. Finally, the real control signal of FACTS devices is calculated according to the selected optimal output through inverse system method. Simulation has been done on a three-machine power system and the results show that the IOSC controller can effectively attenuate system oscillations and enhance the power system transient stability.

articleTitle: Robust H/sub /spl infin// controller design by loop shaping approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper describes the loop shaping design method on the basis of normalized coprime factorization H/sub /spl infin// control theory. The loop shaping approach can gain physical insight in system dynamics, and is effective in tradeoff between performance robustness and stability robustness. The H/sub /spl infin// control theory based upon normalized coprime factorization is concise in expression and high efficient without iteration. Furthermore, the loop shaping design strategy combined with the H/sub /spl infin// control theory has an indicator to know whether the shaping functions are valid or not and point out how to improve the adjustment. The case study on a longitudinal flight control system shows the high efficiency and effectiveness of this methodology.

articleTitle: Fuzzy time Petri nets and its application in supervision of DEDS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A presentation and temporal reasoning method of fuzzy time Petri nets (FTPN) based on linear logic is proposed. FTPN are described by defining the translations in Petri nets using the connectives in linear logic. The behavior of FTPN can be constructed and temporal reasoning can be realized using the rules we defined using linear logic. The method in this paper can be used in fuzzy process supervision and diagnosis in discrete event dynamic systems.

articleTitle: Stability conditions for bi-directional associative memory neural networks with delay
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Bi-directional associative memory (BAM) models are two-layer heteroassociative networks. In the paper, the global asymptotic stability is studied for continuous bi-directional associative memory neural networks with axonal signal transmission delay while the neuronal output signal function S is not differentiable and strictly monotone increasing. Several sufficient conditions guaranteeing the network's global asymptotic stability are derived, the obtained results have important leading significance in the design and application of BAM.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamic system identification based on wavelet approximation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Proposes a multiscale approach for nonlinear dynamic system identification. Based on wavelet multiresolution analysis theory, model parameters are estimated step by step from coarse to finer scales. Some criteria and empirical formulae are discussed that explain how to select initial scale, approximating resolution and size of identification samples. Further, the fundamental frame and identification algorithms of the proposed method are described. The computing complexity and local maximum of neural network methods can be avoided. Finally, the convergence and precision of the identification algorithm are analyzed. The simulating case study on a nonlinear dynamic system shows the high efficiency and effectiveness of this methodology.

articleTitle: A fuzzy control system on industrial evaporation process
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on the analysis of complexity of the industry evaporation process and the difficulty of implementing automatic control over the process, a fuzzy control system with a fuzzy feedforward compensator is designed. The control system mainly consists of an STD industrial computer and frequency converters. The real production shows that using the system can reduce the coal and power consumption, and also improve evaporation quality of the material.

articleTitle: Stability analysis for linear time-varying systems based on generalized orthogonal polynomials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, generalized orthogonal polynomials are directly used to investigate state transition matrix for linear time-varying systems. The approximated series of state transition matrix for such systems is constructed via generalized orthogonal polynomial expansion, and it is shown that the approximated series can retain many properties of state transition matrix under some conditions. Moreover, new criteria of stability for linear time-varying systems are given in terms of the approximated series, the criteria are easier to be tested than the known ones due to the computation advantages via generalized orthogonal polynomials expansion.

articleTitle: An intelligent monitoring system for hazardous waste chemical treatment process
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: An online centralized monitoring system for a hazardous waste chemical treatment process has been designed. The system consists of an online automatic sample system, an automatic cleaning system and an intelligent analysis system. The new system will replace the present tedious and poor human monitoring and off site laboratory analysis in the waste chemical treatment process.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic control, SDR (supervision dialogue report) and infrared ray scan monitoring system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The technology of the computer and new technology of fuzzy logic control are increasingly penetrating and intersecting. In the cement industry fuzzy logic control can be applied to connecting equipment to be renewed continuously, development in the direction of better quality, high production, reliable stability, followed by the development of automatic control technology. We visited two modern cement plants which are a good example of fully automated production lines. The equipment and cement process controlled by computer management system are introduced in Zhu Jiang Cement Plant, Guangzhou.

articleTitle: Material property prediction using neural-fuzzy network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A neural-fuzzy network based adaptive fuzzy modelling approach that includes the initial fuzzy model self-generation, significant input selection, partition validation and parameter optimisation was developed for alloy material property prediction. In this approach, the whole procedure of structure identification and parameter optimisation is carried out automatically and efficiently. The proposed adaptive fuzzy modelling approach has been used to construct composition microstructure property fuzzy models for hot rolled alloy steels. Simulation studies demonstrate that the predicted mechanical properties have good agreement with the measured data by using the obtained fuzzy model with only a few rules.

articleTitle: The mechanism of Java based and objects-oriented simulation on WWW
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper addresses the implementation of a fundamental, easy but powerful mechanism of discrete system simulation on the World Wide Web with Java-based mobile code. With the support of Java multi-thread and object oriented programming theory, this simulation mechanism is different from any other existing simulation modeling language. It is mainly applied on the World Wide Web, and can be easily installed in any Java integrated development environment and extended to more utilized fields, furthermore, virtual reality simulation on WWW, as the further development of this system, is discussed and an M/M/2 queuing system is also given to show the prospects.

articleTitle: A heuristic algorithm for minimizing the range of lateness and makespan on non-identical multiprocessors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A generalized multi-objective model is presented for minimizing the range of lateness and makespan on a multiprocessors job scheduling problem. It is proved that this job scheduling problem is an NP complete problem. So a heuristic algorithm is given to solve the scheduling problem. The numerical example illustrates that the heuristic algorithm is designed very well and can find very good approximate optimal solution.

articleTitle: Research of the algorithm for bipolar analog IC mask recognition based on pattern identification principle
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The bipolar analog IC(B-aIC) holds an important position in the RF IC which is widely used in personal mobile communication. Mask patterns recognition and mask verification of B-aIC are the basis of B-aIC CAD. The authors present a method for B-aIC mask pattern recognition based on the idea of pattern recognition and an expert system (ES). The five elemental mask pattern relationships are defined, the mask description vectors are structured and the algorithm system and the recognition system are organized. The advantage of the algorithm lies in the algorithm being foreign to a specific process, and this makes the recognition fully systemized. An experiment reveals that the algorithm and the recognition are effective, accurate and reliable.

articleTitle: Variable structure process and its control strategy. II. Case study
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, as the variable structure process, the fluidized catalytic cracking unit reactor-regenerator and petroleum distillation column are introduced. For these variable structure processes, the hierarchical control system is a suitable architecture. The application of multivariable predictive coordinated control was illustrated for the control and optimization of these two processes. The advantages of applying the variable structure control to several commercial plants are shown.

articleTitle: Stable adaptive control for nonlinear systems using neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Stability analysis of neural-network-based nonlinear control has presented great difficulties. For a class of affine nonlinear systems with uncertainties, we employed nonlinear-parameter-neural-networks (NPNN) to approximate online the unknown nonlinearities, estimate online the NPNN approximation error's bound, and then succeeded in designing the control law and the adaptive laws of NPNN's weights and the NPNN approximation error's bound. The stability of the closed-loop is proved by using Lyapunov theory. Simulation results show that the controller we proposed exhibits excellent tracking performance.

articleTitle: Generalized synchronization in coupled chaotic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Proposes a simple analytical method for constructing chaotically synchronizing systems in the generalized sense. By using the synchronizing scheme proposed herein, we have realized perfect generalized chaos synchronization in two dimensional coupled maps. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Comparison and analysis of sufficient conditions for fuzzy systems as universal approximators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Different sufficient conditions for Mamdani fuzzy systems and Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy systems as universal approximators are compared and analyzed. With numerical examples, the restrictions, merits and existing defects of these sufficient conditions are discussed.

articleTitle: Study on similarity theory application to PCVR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In the paper, similarity is applied to capture its radiant effect in virtual reality technology. It solves the contradiction of high quality real-time graphics and low cost PC. PCVR technology can be realized at high performance/price ratio.

articleTitle: Optimization problem of shrinkage and thresholding policies in wavelet and the application to image processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The fractional power models for selecting shrinkage and thresholding values are given in wavelet denoising approaches. Some criteria and algorithm for selecting optimal shrinkage and thresholding value are derived through analysing several well-known shrinkage and thresholding policies and use them in 2D signal denoising. The simulation shows that these criteria are useful in the common sense.

articleTitle: Study on using wavelet neural networks for the gait control of a biped robot
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: According to the deficiency in the structure as well as the capability of information storage of the neuron models used in traditional neuron networks, an intelligent neuron assemblage model with generalized wavelet basis function network as its stimulating function is proposed in this paper. The wavelet neural network not only converges much faster with better nonlinear approaching capability, but also is characterized by its ability in variable-scale adaptive structure adjustment and the generalized information storage, etc., which guarantee the network reflects the biological prototype much more faithfully. Static and pseudo dynamic learnings are demonstrated to prove the validity of the proposed mechanism.

articleTitle: Intelligent control and adaptation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)

articleTitle: The identification of head-and-shoulder scene basing on the peculiarity of human vision system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper presents a new identification of head-and-shoulder scene with single color background from the peculiarity of human vision system. It is effective at identifying and is very simple and useful.

articleTitle: A simple method of tip trajectory control for the flexible multi-link manipulator with uncertain parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper studies the tip position trajectory tracking control of a flexible multi-link manipulator. A simple design method of controller is developed based on difference equation and least-mean-squares. Only position measurements are required in the control approach. If the sampling frequency is high enough, some uncertain terms that are difficult to characterize exactly, such as friction, gravity and Coriolis/centripetal terms, can be neglected directly, and the system performance can still be guaranteed. Digital simulation results presented for the flexible two-link manipulator shows that accurate trajectory tracking and vibration damping can be accomplished in the closed-loop system.

articleTitle: A robust VS-MRAC with zero auxiliary errors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A new robust variable structure-model reference adaptive control (VS-MRAC) scheme is presented to deal with plants with the modeled part being relative degree greater than one. The main feature is that all those auxiliary errors of feedback control system can converge to zero in a finite time, thus improves the tracking error.

articleTitle: Optimization and control on separate well and separate zone polymer flooding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In accordance with the complexity of geologic environment in oil fields, the paper presents an optimization model of separate well and separate zone polymer flooding, in which many factors are taken into account, such as the water content of the producing well, polymer injection rate, injection-production ratio, water absorbing capacity, etc. From these factors, constrains are given, and the model is founded and thus realizes the optimization and optimal control on separate well and separate zone polymer flooding. In addition, field application results are provided showing that the model is both practical and advanced.

articleTitle: A synchronous model applied to the distributed multimedia system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a new Petri net model, the prioritized Petri net (P-net). The modeling power and properties of P-nets are analyzed. This model is developed from the object composition Petri net (OCPN) and the extended OCPN (XOCPN). The P-net model is applied to the distributed multimedia synchronization: the distributed object composition Petri net (DOCPN) model. Using the DOCPN model, we can coordinate operations among distributed computer sites.

articleTitle: Perfect self-repairing control for a kind of fault system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The concepts of perfection in a fault system are presented. The design of perfect self-repairing control laws for failures in actuators and in both actuators and sensors are given. The good self-repairing results show the methods are effective.

articleTitle: Semi-decoupled transform and stability analysis for a class of large-scale combined systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In the paper, a semi-decoupled transform is given for large-scale combined systems. According to this result, the stability of the system is discussed. The results are applicable to real problems such as power supply system, lifting system made up of many helicopters, animal living system and so on.

articleTitle: Hidden-layer neuron redundancy-analysis and application in MLP's fault tolerance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Redundancy on hidden-layer neurons has proven useful in the fault tolerance of neural networks. This approach has been applied successfully in the fault tolerance design of classification neural networks, thus the complete single-fault tolerance can be gained. But this approach can only be applied to the feedforward networks which has hard-limit activation functions in output layer. And it prove that this approach is valid only to single-fault. There are universal faults of neurons and weights in actual applications, so we evaluated this approach under universal faults in feedforward networks. We proved that the global fault-rate is reduced though the redundancy on hidden-layer neurons. Then we presented a practical and valid method of redundancy of hidden-layer neurons to gain fault tolerance.

articleTitle: System evaluation using improved superiority analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The superiority analysis based on a connection matrix of gray statistics is an approach that hedges some basic but unnecessary qualifications, so it has been restricted in its application. This paper presents an improved approach of superiority analysis formed by combining connection analysis with the idea of TPOSIS (technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution). It is applicable to general superiority analysis problems with many factors. A practical application of the approach is given to show its feasibility.

articleTitle: An extension to timed colored Petri nets (TCPNs) for modeling manufacturing systems with limited resources availability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper presents an extension to timed colored Petri nets (TCPN) for modeling manufacturing systems subject to the limited availability of some resources. The limited availability of a resource refers to the situation that a resource can only be used within one or more time intervals, which cannot be modeled by the existing TCPN approach. The extension is made by defining the limited usable time stamp, and modifying rules for enabling and firing transitions that have input or output places representing the limited availability of resources. The extended TCPN can be applied in real time control and scheduling of manufacturing systems subject to the limited availability of some resources.

articleTitle: Second order back-propagation learning algorithm and its application for neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, a new second order recursive learning algorithm to multilayer feedforward network is proposed. This algorithm makes not only each layer's errors but also second order derivative information factors backpropagate. And it is proved that it is equivalent to Newton iterative algorithm and has second order convergent speed. New algorithm achieves the recurrence calculation of Newton search directions and the inverse of Hessian matrices. Its calculation complexity corresponds to that of common recursive least squares algorithm. It is stated clearly that this new algorithm is superior to Karayiannis' second order algorithm (1994) according to analysis of their properties.

articleTitle: Asymmetrical relay oscillation based characteristic estimation principle
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, the neglected universal phenomena of asymmetrical relay oscillation are discovered, and the principle of asymmetrical relay oscillation is analyzed and described. The theoretical analysis results have proved that the unbalanced (or generalized) relay loop leads to asymmetrical relay oscillation and symmetrical relay oscillation period is the minimum period in asymmetrical relay oscillation. Then this paper presents the estimation method of symmetrical relay oscillation based on asymmetrical relay oscillation characteristics. Finally, the results of digital simulation and comparison show that the characteristic estimation principle has better estimation effects and wider application prospects.

articleTitle: Robust quadratic stability of interval dynamical system with multiply time-delays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Many systems are interval dynamical systems (IDS) with multiply time-delays, such as chemical processes and flight systems. In fact, most researches on stability analysis for IDS with time-delays are quite conservative. To improve the existing results, new methods of analyzing the robust quadratic stability of IDS with multiply time-delays are proposed. First, the convention form of IDS with multiply time-delays is transformed into a certain structured form, which is equal to the former and can be analyzed conveniently. Then, a delay-independent criterion is developed for IDS with multiply time invariant delays. By solving a Riccati inequality, a sufficient condition based on Lyapunov stability theory for quadratic stability of the system was obtained. Finally, the proposed methods are extended to apply to IDS with multiply time varying delays.

articleTitle: The principle and structure of an intelligent and highly stable gyro power supply
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper introduces the principle and structure of an intelligent and highly stable gyro power supply, and the chief test results obtained in our lab are reported.

articleTitle: Virtual-clock phase space in synchronous control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The skew problem between the clocks and signals and the VLSI design methodology for virtual-clock in high speed control chips are considered in this paper. Both the lumped parameter and distributed parameter are used simultaneously in this technique to construct the virtual-clock space. Thereby the end user can adjust the clock phase smoothly in a wide enough scope to best match the corresponding signals.

articleTitle: High performance SPWM frequency converter three-phase cage induction motor's synchronous modulation variable frequency speed regulation system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper discusses the synchronous modulation model of the SPWM frequency converter three-phase cage induction motor's variable frequency speed regulation system at the carrier ratio of N=27. The fundamental frequency and mechanical characteristic parameters are calculated according to the parameters of the T801-4 motor. The result obtained show that its microcomputer control system is simple, the mechanical characteristic is robust and the motor was running steadily at low speed as the result of a high performance variable frequency and speed regulation.

articleTitle: A neural network fuzzy comprehensive evaluation for evaluating economic benefit of business firm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A method of fuzzy multiple comprehensive evaluation of economic benefit of business firm is proposed, which uses artificial neural network to analyze the weights of evaluation indices of economic benefit. In this way, the economic benefit of business firm can be analyzed and evaluated more directly and reasonably. A practical example is also given.

articleTitle: Applying Lie series in the singular optimal controls
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: We study in this paper the singular optimal control problems. We derive the basic formulation and obtain a sufficient and necessary condition for singular optimal controls. Meanwhile, we approximate the solution by Lie series and present a computational method to deal with the optimization.

articleTitle: Real time analysis on expert systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In some comprehensive systems, as decisive loops, expert systems make up the whole system, so much more studies on reasoning time are necessary. The reasoning time in an expert system relates to its reasoning mode, its knowledge base architecture, the performance of the computer and the support languages. The paper takes the knowledge base architecture as an example to study the reasoning time. Finally, a temporally homogeneous Markov chain is used to model the knowledge base. The time estimating mathematics model and the computation method are also given, which can provide proofs for the comprehensive system control and real time simulation.

articleTitle: A new hybrid genetic method for establishing a neural network model of the boiling sugar crystalization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The backpropagation and simplex are the classical search methods, so both are easily entrapped in a local optimum. To solve this problem, we develop a new hybrid genetic algorithm that is based on the probabilistic simplex and backpropagation. Moreover, we have established a neural network model of the boiling sugar crystallization. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method is very effective.

articleTitle: Reduced order modeling in time-frequency H/sub /spl infin//-norm mix-criterion: genetic algorithms approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The reduced order modeling in time-frequency least squares mix-criterion is proposed, and the method based on genetic algorithms is obtained to resolve it. This new method avoids the shortfall of the traditional methods, and the characteristics of the reduced order model obtained are ideal. An example shows that this method is better than other available methods.

articleTitle: Analysis and modelling of a class of generalized fuzzy operators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper discusses a class of generalized fuzzy operators named as the generalized probability sum operator and the generalized probability product operator, which have been proposed by authors for fuzzy reasoning. Here we further analyze their characters from theory. A proof that two operators belonged to T-norm and T-conorm separately is given. And a fuzzy neural network model based on the operators is constructed. The model could be used for fuzzy inference or fuzzy control.

articleTitle: Using nonlinear regression method in oil production prediction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Weng's cycle model is a typical oil production prediction model. Traditionally a linear regression method is used to simulate the model. It brings some limitation on the regression accuracy so in this paper we use nonlinear regression instead of linear regression. The new method is used in an oil production field and good results are obtained.

articleTitle: Improvement on the generation methods of pseudo-randoms on the military modelling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on a detailed analysis of the generation method of pseudo-randoms in military modelling, the authors put forward a better way to improve the generation methods and make a comparative test on it.

articleTitle: Design and control of flexible transfer system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)

articleTitle: The development of multimedia monitoring system for the railway road condition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Railway track condition monitoring is necessary to ensure the safety of train running. Author developed monitoring system for track condition. It can be fitted in an existing railway checking carriage. It uses data collection and multimedia technology. The article discusses the system's structure, the selection of hardware and software, the method used in developing it, key routes, and methods of applying the system.

articleTitle: Petri net based AUV modeling and analyzing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: By analyzing the features such as asynchronism, concurrency and event-driven control of the autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) system, the concepts of basic procedure, concurrent procedure and parallel procedure are proposed. In addition, the authors define operators such as sequence, loop, selection, condition, conditional loop, parallel, synchronous concurrency and concurrent communication, whose Petri net representations are also given. Accordingly, the authors propose a novel modeling method of the AUV based on Petri net. On the basis of the above work, the broadcasting module, perceptional module, planing module and control module are constructed using a bottom-up approach. Finally, a synchronous model is developed and an analysis of the model of the AUV system is given.

articleTitle: Fuzzy feedback linearization control for nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on the T-S fuzzy model, a design method for a fuzzy feedback linearization system is investigated. For systems with uncertainties, a sufficient condition to make closed system L/sub 2/-stabilization is proposed using the small gain theorem, and the bound of uncertainties is given. The simulation shows the fuzzy feedback linearization is a valid method to control nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: A kind of robust adaptive controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper studies a class of linear system with uncertainty of parameters and external time-varying input disturbances. A united real-time identification method is presented for estimating the parameters and external disturbances of the system at the same time without the model of disturbance. The disturbance is compensated online according to the results of identification. A dual adaptive controller is designed. This controller can rejected the effect of uncertainty of parameters and eliminates the bad phenomena of conventional adaptive control systems, such as "turn off", "windup" and "bursting", so the robustness of the adaptive control system is enhanced. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is proved by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Optimal design of operating procedures for chemical processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In order to design more operable or even optimal chemical processes, a reliability theory is proposed to support the planning of operating procedures. The optimality can be achieved through the quantification, thoroughness, practicability, safety and energy conservation considerations of this methodology. A three-tier reasoning framework is constructed to describe the two-step quantitative planning strategy. The first step is the optimal operating path determination and the second step is the optimal primitive operations generation. This paper presents a knowledge-model (KM) method in which an expert knowledge base is combined with the process dynamic model to obtain an optimal operating path. Finally, the methodology is illustrated by an example of the temperature increasing procedure for a subsystem of charge gas dehydrator regeneration in an ethylene plant.

articleTitle: A multi-factorial decision-making model for deduction of rules in rough sets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Rough set theory is a new mathematical tool to deal with vagueness and uncertainty. It has been used in machine learning, knowledge discovery, decision support systems and pattern recognition. Traditionally, the algorithm to obtain the deduction of decision rule in rough sets theory always take into account the number of decision rules more than their cost. In this paper, we introduce how to reconcile the conflict of the simplicity and the cost of rules by using multiple objective decision-making (MOD), and the efficiency and effectiveness of rough set can be improved.

articleTitle: A closed-loop D-type iterative learning control law for discrete linear uncertain systems and its application to electrohydraulic servo systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, a closed-loop D-type iterative learning control scheme for the precise tracking control of a class of discrete linear uncertainty systems is presented. The conditions, which guarantee the convergence of the scheme, are given and then proved. Subsequently, this paper described the application of this scheme in the field of electrohydraulic servo systems. Simulations show that the good result has been obtained using this scheme.

articleTitle: Decision control system on picking optimal speech from multi-channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A decision control system for picking optimal speech from multi-channels based on quality assessment is presented. First, the feature parameters which are used to describe speech quality are extracted on the basis of analyzing the properties of remote speech communication channels. Second, an objective assessment model of speech quality is founded. Finally, a decision control system has been developed combined with properties of human beings. This decision control system can ensure that communication should be carried on the best speech channel, as well as it can also keep a good audio performance during switching. This system has been applied in practice successfully and the performance of it is very satisfactory.

articleTitle: Relative equilibria of power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the relative equilibria of the excitation control of power systems. It is shown that the systems have no common conservative quantity for both the unforced system and closed-loop system. It implies that the closed-loop system has different conservative quantity from the unforced system, i.e., it has no relative equilibrium to the power system.

articleTitle: The wide-range impulse robust output feedback control of generalized systems with structured perturbations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The impulse robust output feedback control problem of generalized uncertain linear systems with structured perturbations is discussed. When the ideal system of the uncertain systems can normalize the system by output, and the uncertain structured parameters are all known, the wide-range impulse robust output feedback controllers and their designed strategy are obtained by use of the matrix algebraic method. In addition, the uncertainties can easily be determined and the robust controllers can easily be realized. An illustrative example is given to show the control method described is practical.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis of performance for semi-Markov processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A stochastic process is a fundamental research model for discrete event dynamic systems. In this paper, we studied the problems of sensitivity analysis of the steady-state performance for a class of semi-Markov processes by using the potential theory. We gave the sensitivity formulas of the steady-state performance expressed by the potentials of systems. These formulas can be directly used in studying the problems of controlling and optimization of systems.

articleTitle: Robust control design for uncertain sampled-data system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Presents the robust controller design method for sampled-data control system with uncertainty in both system matrix and control matrix. Based on the robust design method for a continuous system, two sufficient conditions are developed for the existence of the robust controller for uncertain sampled-data systems.

articleTitle: A cascade control system of exit temperature of drum-type asphalt concrete mixing machinery by a fuzzy RBF networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper lays its study emphasis on the exit temperature control of drum-type asphalt concrete mixing machinery. Firstly, a simplified model of fuzzy radial basis function (RBF) neural network is presented and its structure and clustering algorithm of hidden nodes are analyzed in detail. Secondly, a fuzzy cascade control system is designed by this model and its self-learning algorithm in cascade form is discussed. Finally, a lot of computer simulations are done to verify the validity and feasibility of the control method and the self-learning algorithm presented in this paper. The results of simulations show that the fuzzy cascade control system is in possession of high control accuracy and adaptivity.

articleTitle: Oscillation of a class of delay 2-D discrete dynamic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Delay 2-D discrete dynamic systems, that is, partial difference equation. It is studying for a news domain on the qualitative theory of delay partial difference equation. The paper is concerned with two partial difference equations of the form A/sub m-1,n/+A/sub m,n-1/-pA/sub mn/+qA/sub m+k,n+l/=0 and A/sub m-1,n/+A/sub m,n-1/-A/sub mn/+u//spl Sigma//i=1p/sub 1/(m,n)A/sub m+k,n+l/=0 respectively. We obtain sufficient conditions for the oscillation of all solutions of these equations.

articleTitle: Description method of the state machine for industry control chips
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In the field of industrial control, the design of the state machine is very important to the quality of CMOS chips. The description of state machine is the central of its design on HDL (hardware description language). According to the graphology in mathematical induction, this paper introduces a new rule to classify the description method. The structural framework of the state machine and its principle are analysed. Finally, we discuss the applications to the source code compiling, reading and simulation.

articleTitle: Compound fuzzy adaptive control for nonlinear process with delay
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper focuses on nonlinear plants with long dead-time and unknown parameters which are dependent on known variables. A compound fuzzy adaptive controller is proposed which is based on Smith predictor and model-reference adaptation. Different with the theoretical robust controllers for nonlinear plants with time delays, the controller has good engineering generality and is easy to implement. High dynamical performance can be obtained for the control system, as well as the stability and convergence properties are theoretically proofed.

articleTitle: An on-line Chinese signature verification system using an impulse response of signature generation model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Chinese signature verification is the leading edge in the field of Chinese information processing. This paper presents a function method for signature verification using an impulse response of signature generation model, which is more strict than the parameter method that is used widely. In order to avoid high order inverse matrix calculating, an approach of segmentation proceed with the administrative levels of Chinese character frames, and stroke-based segmentation is used. So that an impulse response of signature generation model can be used for signature verification. The experiments reveal the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Trace data association with artificial neural network improved classified principle
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Artificial neural network ART model with improved classified principle is applied to trace data association of air target. The model with improved similitude classified principle avoids the incorrect result of trace data association by directly using ART model in some special situation. In the end of the paper, the simulation result is presented.

articleTitle: A system theoretic foundation for blind system identification and estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)

articleTitle: The HMRAC scheme with arbitrary relative orders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The hybrid model reference adaptive control (HMRAC) system with arbitrary relative orders has been designed. The scope of the paper by Wu et al. (1986) has been expanded. The non-minimum phase problem of digitizing the system has been avoided.

articleTitle: FCC process modeling and light oil yield optimization research
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The fluidized catalystic cracking (FCC) is the most important secondary processing technique in oil refining industry. The authors use the multilayer forward neural network for identifying and establishing the model of FCC reaction process, and the self-correlation function in checking the reliability of the model. In the research of light oil yield optimization the authors develop a series of optimization steps from both the Frank-Wolfe algorithm and approximation programming. The use of this method with real production data can lead to a satisfactory result. It is feasible to apply this optimization method into the coordinator controller in the step-up control system of the light oil production. Adjusting the online industrial procedure parameters according to the optimization object, the coordinator controller can make the whole system run on an optimal state and enhance the yield of light oil.

articleTitle: Acquiring knowledge from data by clustering and optimum-seeking
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach of knowledge acquisition from domain data, which named clustering and optimum-seeking. It offers a complete solution of KDD application to quality control of industrial enterprises. It is applied in practice, and proved effective.

articleTitle: Observer-based robust fault-tolerant control of uncertain systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: An observer-based robust fault-tolerant control problem is studied for a class of uncertain systems. The uncertainty does not satisfy matching conditions and is value bounded. Using linear matrix inequalities, a sufficient condition for observer-based stabilization feedback robust control laws is presented in the case of actuator failures.

articleTitle: Supervisory control of extended timed event graph
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper describes the dynamic behavior of extended timed event graphs (ETEG) related to place delay in the dioid framework. By Cofer and Garg's supervisory control theory (1996), we address control problems of extended timed event graphs. Supervisory control of extended timed event graphs (a class of discrete event dynamic systems) is studied in the dioid framework. A necessary and sufficient condition for the ideals of the set of firing time sequences of transitions to be controllable is presented. We prove all the strongly controllable subsets can form a complete lattice.

articleTitle: Robust guidance law for space interception
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In space interception, a linear time-varying model is established to describe the missile-target related line-of-sight (LOS) motion, where the guidance parameter variations and target maneuvers are regarded as gain bounded disturbances. From this model, a robust guidance law of homing-missile is derived and its robustness against the gain bounded uncertainty is proved by Lyapunov-like approach. Simulation results obtained demonstrate the effectiveness of the presented guidance method.

articleTitle: An approach for the design of supervisory controller of discrete event systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper describes a new method for the synthesis of Petri net based supervisory control for discrete event system (DES) by blocking or enabling controllable transitions in the system according to the forbidden state specifications. The supervisory control methodology is proposed to provide such a formal technique for the modeling, specification, simulation and simplification of supervisory control for DES in a very simple and compact way.

articleTitle: Research of the application of intelligent fuzzy control in high rate hydraulic machine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Makes a study of an intelligent fuzzy control strategy in a high rate hydraulic machine and the design of software and hardware of the intelligent control, and introduces the outcomes of some experiments. Theoretical analysis and experimental outcome show that for the high rate hydraulic machine predictive fuzzy control is a perfect intelligent control method.

articleTitle: Existence of positive definite solution to periodic Riccati differential equation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper deals with the standard periodic Riccati differential equation. A complete necessary and sufficient condition is presented for the existence of Hermitian periodic positive definite (HPPD) solution. Previously, after a proper change of basis in the state space the condition can be expressed in terms of the notions of stabilizability and detectability. Moreover, it is shown that when a HPPD solution exists, it is either unique, or else there are uncountably many such solutions. The result of the paper can be considered as a valid extension of Richardson and Kwong's (1986) result to the periodic version.

articleTitle: Intelligent online measurement instrument of opening force
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The intelligent online measurement instrument of a washer-clutch's opening force is based on a single chip computer system with a force sensor of resistance strain gauges and auto-localization equipment. The paper presents the design method of an adaptive compensation measuring system in the dynamic measurement of transfer function. It makes the measuring force track the acting force, as well as improve measuring accuracy.

articleTitle: An expert fuzzy controller used for silit tube pipe furnace with high temperature
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper are analyzed the specific properties of the silit tube pipe furnace and the demand for it. The characteristics of the silit tube pipe furnace are nonlinearity and long time lag. Secondly, the expert system for intelligent control is introduced into the fuzzy control in accordance with the characteristics. The expert fuzzy controller is developed. The control rule is given. The advantages of the expert fuzzy controller are given, together with problems needing further study.

articleTitle: Model validation of multirate systems from time-domain experimental data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The validation problem using time-domain experimental data is studied for multirate linear fractional uncertain models. First we give the necessary and sufficient conditions to the Caratheodory-Fejer interpolation problem with nest operator constraints. The validation tests are then given based on the above conditions and the lifting technique. Tractable convex optimization methods can be used to solve the validation problems.

articleTitle: Micromachined piezoelectric traveling wave micromotors for intelligent systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper described a new type of thick films piezoelectric rotary micromotor, whose stator is made from a commercially available piezoelectric membrane composed of a copper substrate to which piezoelectric ceramics PZT thick films are bonded. This micromotor was driven by the traveling wave formed by the combination of two standing wave natural flexural waves whose phases differ by 90/spl deg/, spatially and temporally. Then, a novel rotor structure, with protrusions on the contact surface, was designed and fabricated by silicon wet etching. The stator was obtained by standard photolithography. Next, using the power source we developed, some properties of the micromotor were measured and analyzed. Unlike the other motors, no extra force was applied to the rotor of our motor. The frictional force between the rotor and stator can be adjusted by changing the rotor weight and the protrusion configuration. It is shown that a rotation speed of up to 50 rpm under the exciting voltage 10 V was achieved.

articleTitle: The study and realization of SCADA system in manufacturing enterprises
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The key technologies of SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition) system in manufacturing enterprises, such as the database and client server structure, are discussed in this paper. The realization of the system is also given. Finally, the authors forecast the development trend in this field.

articleTitle: Rough set theory and its practice in knowledge discovery
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: As an effective mathematical tool to deal with vagueness and uncertainty, the rough set theory has got much attention in the fields of artificial intelligence, pattern recognition, knowledge process and so on. This paper introduces the Pawlak rough set theory model (1992, 1995) and the generalized rough set theory model, discusses the general methods used in knowledge discovery in database, and measures the plausibility with the generalized model. Finally, it also reviews the research and applications briefly.

articleTitle: The BP neural network algorithm and the model of the reliability growth predication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The reliability growth prediction is the most important part of the reliability engineering. This paper considers the backpropagation (BP) algorithm application in reliability growth prediction. The Gompertz model is a good reliability growth model. The paper examines the BP algorithm and compares it with the Gompertz model. The results show that they were both basically consistent. It indicates that the BP approach is feasible, effective, simple and adaptive. This paper also discusses the prediction of the reliability storage in the weapon system using the BP algorithm.

articleTitle: Neuron controller with adaptive regulated gain for paper machine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper-making process is very complex, there exists long delay time, grievous nonlinearities and time-varying parameters. The paper presents a neuron model-free control method in which the neuron gain is regulated adaptively for the paper-making process. This procedure can control the process with long delay time and great range of open-loop gain variation efficiently. The simulation results for a complex paper machine is satisfying, good performances in robustness and adaptability are obtained.

articleTitle: The application research on TMN platform with CORBA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper described the specifications and functions of TMN (telecommunication management network) and CORBA (the common object request broker architecture) first. And then, we provided one contribution to research the application on TMN with CORBA according to the object-oriented technique and distributed processing technique.

articleTitle: A fault diagnosis expert system for hydraulic system of injection moulding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Injection moulding is a kind of highly automatic machine. The hydraulic system is an important part for its proper operation. But because of the frequent faults, the productivity of injection moulding is significantly decreased. Traditionally, the expert system for fault diagnosis is only based on expert experiences. However, considering the complexity of faults of the hydraulic system, it sometimes leads to inaccurate results, even no results. We present a method based on the combination of an expert's experiences and the object's structure and function. By using shallow and deep knowledge synthetically, the framework of an efficacious system is proposed. We describe the generalized knowledge base and the new diagnosis strategies and reference mechanism. We also give some practical rules in LISP language. In most cases, especially unexpected ones, this method can lead to better results.

articleTitle: Development of CAD platform for an practical AC speed-adjusting system based on Device Net
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The development of a CAD platform and its significance for future research are introduced. The platform is for research of a practical AC speed-adjusting system based on Device Net. Through monitoring the Device Manager which is developed by Rockwell Software, it can obtain the voltage, current etc. of the motor to be controlled, and this provides great convenience for future employment of a fuzzy neural network to estimate the rotor speed of the motor and implement a speed sensorless motor control.

articleTitle: The improved learning rule of neuron and its application in the servo controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A neuron is a basic unit of neural network. The learning process will certainly be effected by different learning rules. According to the learning ways of neuron, this paper presents a modified method, which is based on the guide factor, for the learning rule of neuron. The improved rule is applied to the design of a neural controller for a servo system. Simulation results show the presented method can improve the robust performance and tracking process of the system.

articleTitle: A cascaded neural network and its application to modelling power plant pollutant emission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Pollutant emission in power generation plant, especially NOx emission, has attracted much attention in the last ten years. For an operating plant, development of an advanced control system is essential for pollutant emission reduction. System modelling is an important stage in emission control. In this paper, a cascading neural network is used to model the NOx emission in a coal-fired power generation plant. This type of neural network has more connections than that found in the layered feedforward neural network. Algorithm for training this type of neural network is suggested and then it is used to build a NOx emission model for a coal-fired power generation plant. Simulation results show the merits of this type of neural network.

articleTitle: Nonlinear system identification with genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on the genetic algorithm and Volterra series model, a new identification method of nonlinear systems is proposed. The method is adapted to the difference magnitude of parametric of model. An adaptation algorithm is developed in order to get a wider search range and achieve more accurate solutions synchronously. With unique mutation and selection, an effective genetic algorithm is achieved for solving the identification of nonlinear systems. The simulation and experimental results indicate that the new method achieved high accuracy, robustness and adaptability.

articleTitle: On the robust stability of general Lurie control systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The Lyapunov function method is used to study the robust absolute stability of general interval Lurie control systems, and algebraic sufficient conditions are obtained for the general interval Lurie type control systems. A relationship between the stability of the symmetric interval matrix and robust absolute stability of general interval Lurie type control systems is established.

articleTitle: Streptomycin fermentation process modeling with principal component analysis and fuzzy model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Analysis, modeling and control for a fed-batch fermentation process still remain challenging issues. Based on principal component analysis (PCA) and fuzzy modelling a simple and efficient approach to monitoring fed-batch streptomycin fermentation is presented. The data obtained from an industrial streptomycin fermentation process is first analyzed with PCA so that the large multivariate data with highly correlated and noisy measurements can be compressed into a lower dimension space which contains most of the variance of the original matrix. Moreover, a fuzzy model is used to construct a product (antibiotic) concentration estimator of the streptomycin fermentation process, prior knowledge and expertise are important in fed-batch fermentation processes. The results of the fuzzy model compared with a linear multivariate regression model indicate the potential of the fuzzy model as a state estimator of all such industrial fed-batch processes.

articleTitle: Analysis and systematic design method of fuzzy controllers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper applied a new asymmetrical, all-folded triangular-shaped membership function of the input variable to design the fuzzy controller. Based on these, we developed the structure analysis of the typical fuzzy controller with two inputs and one output and gave the output expressions of the fuzzy controllers with five fuzzy sets for fuzzification. Then we proposed a systematic design method of fuzzy control systems based on the existing PI/PD controllers. The simulation result shows the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Image classification based on data fusion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The purpose of the paper is to advance the performance of the multisource remotely sensed images classification. A new conception of the classification is proposed by using the idea of the intelligent engineering and advanced method of data fusion. Image classification used by data fusion based on the statistical method is achieved and some helpful conclusions are discussed. The experiments show that the new method is superior to the traditional methods and the augmented vector approach.

articleTitle: Multivariable intelligent decoupling control and its applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)

articleTitle: An exploration of quasi-sliding mode VS-MRAC strategy for discrete-time and time-varying linear SISO systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper presents a new method for adaptive control of time-varying plants with time delay. It combines the model reference adaptive control (MRAC) strategy with quasi-sliding mode variable structure control strategy, and obtains a good control quality. Furthermore, a quasi-sliding VS strategy for discrete-time is also derived so that the algorithm can be used to realize the numerical control. The theoretical and simulation results show that the presented algorithm is valid and efficient.

articleTitle: The advanced control and optimization in tobacco strips processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper introduces briefly the tobacco strips processing procedure, pointing out the economical and social benefits. It lists the theories of the online adaptive optimization and the generalized predictive control algorithm. The control and optimization schemes are implemented on an advanced adaptive control and optimization workstation. Through the system reconstruction and software configuration, the workstation can be integrated into the existing computer monitoring system. The schemes aims at increasing the filling density of tobacco strips and controlling the water content percentage on the set-point within the permitted bound.

articleTitle: Real-time time-optimal control of manipulators based on gravity center motion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Fast motion is a central problem in high-performance robotics. Finding the minimum time control strategies for point to point operation of a robotic manipulator is algorithmically difficult and computationally very intensive. As a result, the practical applicability of currently available methods is very limited. In this study, we present an approximate solution to the time-optimal trajectory planning problem, from a point of view of the gravity center motion. While not producing the exact minimum-time solution, the algorithm approximated the minimum-time solution can be easily utilized online. The algorithm running on a typical PC computer only takes about 1.03 seconds, while the algorithm for the exact time optimal solution takes about 2.54 seconds. It is thus possible for real-time control.

articleTitle: Decoupling control by traced method of strong coupling system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper proposes a control method to decouple strongly coupled systems through main and auxiliary circus tracing. It is shown from simulation results, that it has a good effect in the uniform control of the temperature field of a strongly coupled system.

articleTitle: Algorithms of sparselization based on feedforward neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In order to sparselize feedforward neural networks, "topological sort" and "partial order" are introduced, then a self-constructing learning algorithm and a self-adjusting pruning algorithm are presented. It is necessary to modify existing connections and create new connections. Experimental results show they can prune redundant neurons and connections with good performance.

articleTitle: The design of full response sliding mode variable structure robust controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, a design method of full response sliding mode variable structure robust controller is introduced. The design steps of switching surface and the process of control are described in detail. The simulation example illustrates the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Robust controller design for a class of nonlinear systems with mismatched uncertainties
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The problem of robust stabilization for a class of mismatched uncertain nonlinear systems is considered. The required information about uncertainties in the system is merely that the uncertainties are bounded in a Euclidean norm by a known function of the system states. It can be viewed as an extension of the work in Qu (1994). First, the uncertainties are decomposed into matched and mismatched parts. Then based on a Lyapunov method, a robust controller is proposed, which will compensate matched and mismatched uncertainties respectively. In contrast with some previous controllers which can only guarantee practical stability of the systems, the robust controller presented in the paper can guarantee that the resulting closed-loop systems are globally asymptotically stable. The simulation result shows that the method suggested is effective.

articleTitle: Modified DMC method and its realization based on BP neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Presents a modified dynamic matrix control (DMC) algorithm and its realization based on BP neural networks with higher nonlinear mapping and learning ability, predictive precision is increased and the control quality is improved by this control algorithm. In addition, the predictive control algorithm is extended to nonlinear systems. The results of simulation show that this algorithm is simple and applicable; its robustness is high; the transient and steady-state quality and the oscillation of the control variable are improved.

articleTitle: The FNN control and its application to chemical fiber industry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A fuzzy neural network control strategy is presented. Fuzzy rules are optimized when the strategy is used to control side-wind for chemical fiber which require constant temperature, constant humidity and constant air velocity. The feature of the algorithm is introduced, and this method is proved feasible by simulation.

articleTitle: The design of bus arbitration chip based on the dynamic and static mixture algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The bus arbiter chip has been widely used in many fields of industry control. An excellent arbitration algorithm, the dynamic and static mixture algorithm, is described in this paper. The design method of this algorithm is introduced in detail, and the Verilog HDL description is also given. The dynamic and static mixture algorithm is a two-level arbitration algorithm, which gives attention to equality as well as priority. This algorithm is of reference value in the design of industrial bus arbiter chip, as well as in other systems.

articleTitle: Personified intelligent control for an inverted pendulum system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The concept of "personalized intelligent control" is illustrated in this paper. Not based on accurate mathematical model, personified intelligent control method forms control laws directly by means of qualitative analysis and synthesis of the plant. We apply it successfully to balancing of an inverted pendulum system, which is a classic example of an inherently nonlinear unstable system. The experimental results show the feasibility, effectiveness and robustness of the applied controller.

articleTitle: Research on full digital electric control system of heavy boring machine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A full digital electric control system of heavy boring machine is introduced. The control problems of the full digital DC drive of the control system are discussed and methods of improving the system are offered. The analysis results are verified by computer simulation.

articleTitle: A new approach of halftoning based on error diffusion with rough set filtering
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The rough set filtering makes use of the concepts of indiscernibility relations and approximation spaces to define an equivalence class of neighboring pixels in a processing mask, then utilize the statistical mean of the equivalence classes to replace the gray levels of the central pixel in a processing mask. The error diffusion makes use of the correction factor composed of the weighted errors for these pixels prior to addition of the pixel to be processed to diffuse error over the neighboring pixels in a continuous tone image. Both of a system and an algorithm of implementation of halftoning on error diffusion with rough sets are introduced in the paper.

articleTitle: A research of FL neural network for fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: FL network architecture is a supervised learning extension of the BP network method we have studied thus far. It allows specification of the category into which inputs will be classified. In the designated category, the training set is extended into the input pattern of single layer perceptron with nonlinear change. It is high efficient in the aspects of processing speed and avoiding local stability, and especially useful in fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Improved independence and fault-tolerance of INS/GNSS integrated navigation system by SAR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a type of radar capable of generating very high resolution images of ground based objects and working independently. For the problem of INS/GNSS integrated navigation system this paper fuses a sensor of SAR with it to improve its independence, fault-tolerance and navigation precision. The simulation results prove that SAR advances this system's performance. Meanwhile, the attitude stability of SAR antenna is enhanced. SAR images and the integrated system's precision are improved. So INS/GNSS/SAR integrated navigation system is of high performance with high fault-tolerance.
