articleTitle: Research on application of recurrent neural network in modelling jigging system of coal preparation plant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Recurrent neural network can describe complex nonlinear time-varying dynamic system. In this paper, model and unified mathematical description of recurrent neural network are presented. The BP algorithm to train this network is also presented. Finally, this network is applied to model jigging system of coal preparation plant. An example shows that this network has strong capability in dynamic approach.

articleTitle: Expert fault diagnosis using rule models with certainty factors for the leaching process
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A key point in the operation of the leaching process is to ensure the safe running of the process. The paper proposes an expert fault diagnosis strategy for the leaching process, which is based on rule models with certainty factors. A diagnosis procedure is first presented. Then, the rule models are constructed based on empirical knowledge, empirical data and statistical results on past fault countermeasures, and an expert reasoning method is used which employs the rule models and forward chaining. A real-word application is expounded finally.

articleTitle: The application of elitist preserved genetic algorithms on fuzzy controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: We design the fuzzy controller of a double-inverted pendulum based on the fuzzy set theory, and derive the parameters of the controller in an application of the elitist preserved genetic algorithms. The result of the simulation shows that this is a valid method to design the fuzzy controller of the system that has multiple inputs and multiple outputs.

articleTitle: A cleaner production strategy for pulp and paper processes based multi-agent
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A cleaner production strategy for processes in pulp and paper industries is investigated which considers the combination of technology and equipment with a processes control method. A multi-agent structure is applied to build the models of pulping and papermaking processes. The model structure and implementation of this strategy is discussed. The strategy based on multi-agents provides an idea to study and analyze integrated optimization of complex control systems.

articleTitle: Using computer to simulate the movement of plane link mechanism dynamically
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Desribes the use of the object in Visual Basic to describe the components that compose a plane link mechanism, and using an OOP method to realize the movement parameter of the components in the program. The dimension and position in different moments of components are displayed on the computer screen exactly proportionally. So the movements of the mechanism are simulated by the computer dynamically.

articleTitle: Nonlinear reconfigurable control based on RBF neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A new type of nonlinear reconfigurable control strategy based on model-following method using radial basis function (RBF) neural networks is presented in this paper. This method can make the outputs of an impaired system track those of reference model accurately without knowing the location and damage degree of failure, and a RBF neural network controller is used to compensate nonlinear dynamics caused by failure; simulation results reveal that this method has good reconfigurable performance and robustness.

articleTitle: A genetic algorithm for constrained optimization in simultaneous stabilizing problem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper proposes a new constrained optimization algorithm after concisely surveying the constraint handling method in genetic algorithm. Traditional genetic algorithm is improved and the new algorithm is used for solving the simultaneous stabilizing control problem. Some other concepts, either superior to or equivalence to genetic algorithms, are used for comparison. It is shown that the algorithm can systematically handle constraints and it needs neither aiding penalty functions nor feasible initial solutions in producing infeasible solutions. Comparison of experimental results and numerical simulation show that the algorithm has good performance and can effectively solve simultaneous stabilizing problem.

articleTitle: Fuzzy reasoning based on genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, a kind of fuzzy reasoning based on genetic algorithms (GA) is introduced. The fuzzy reasoning system uses genetic algorithms to adjust weights of all reasoning rules synthetically. At last, the results of computer simulations also reveal that GA is effective and practical in optimizing those weights.

articleTitle: Modeling complex systems by abstraction and formalization approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Models play key roles in analyzing and studying complex systems in the objective world. The most important relations between a real system and its model are abstraction and mapping, which make up the basis of modeling process. In practice, it is advantageous and sometime essential to formalize and canonize systems models, because the normalized models are easy to use and analyze theoretically. This paper describes some abstraction and formalization ideas for modeling complex systems.

articleTitle: Multipurpose virtual-reality-based motion simulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Public security has become an important issue everywhere. Especially, the safe manipulation and control of various machines and vehicles has gained special attention such that the authorities keep emphasizing the strict training and censoring of human operators. Currently, such training and censoring process usually relies on the actual machines, equipment, or vehicles in the real sites. This not only has high demands in space, time and cost, but also causes another public security problem. In this connection, the world-wide trend is to tackle the above dilemma by using virtual reality (VR). However, the current researches or products on VR are more matured in the software display part of VR. How to combine 3D VR display with motion platform to achieve the aforementioned training and censoring purposes is an important research issue. This paper focuses on this research issue, and the goal is to develop a multipurpose virtual-reality-based motion simulation system to meet the requirements of public security in training and censoring of human operators.

articleTitle: Design of slave computer under micro-operating robot
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A micro-operating robot is an important research field in intelligent robots. The article discusses design of hardware and implementation of software in a slave computer under a micro-operating robot. We also carried out experiments on the cell's conveying system. The results show that our system is stable and reliable.

articleTitle: Several results on Triple I algorithm with totally inference rules of fuzzy reasoning
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The theory of the Triple 1 algorithm with total inference rules for the implication operator R/sub 0/ is further discussed. Based on the theory of sustained degree together with the formulas of /spl alpha/-Triple 1 MP and /spl alpha/-Triple 1 MT of an algorithm given in the literature, we propose the theory of the restricted degree of the Triple 1 algorithm, analyse its properties and obtain general formulas of supremum of /spl alpha/-Triple 1 MP and infimum of /spl alpha/-Triple 1 MT.

articleTitle: Dynamic neural network based nonlinear adaptive control for a distillation column
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, a dynamic neural network is used to learn the input-output behaviors of a binary distillation column by combining the mechanistic property. The model can be online identified. The weight-training algorithm is proposed. The convergence of the algorithm is discussed by using the Lyapunov method. Based on the identified model, a nonlinear adaptive controller is designed, which can preserve the stability and robustness of the closed loop system. Some simulation results are illustrated to show the effectiveness of the controller.

articleTitle: The dynamic task scheduling in the multiprocessor system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The distributed multiprocessor system is increasingly applied in the equipment management of many kinds of vehicles (such as aircraft, ship et.). How to ensure the mission reliability of multiprocessor system is a key technology in these applications. In the paper, a task scheduling algorithm is illustrated, which is based on distributed processing. Through the tasks migrating among nodes in the system, the mission reliability of the multiprocessor system is raised. The algorithm resides in each node. The tradeoff between the optimum scheme and computation cost is made. The algorithm is so simple that the advantages of a distributed multiprocessor system is brought into play. The flexibility is proved through scheduling experiments. The performance ratio of the algorithm satisfies the requirement of vehicles.

articleTitle: The design of optimum neuron controllers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A method of obtaining optimum neuron controllers for minimization of the integral of time weight absolute error (ITAE) criteria and integral of the squared error (ISE) criteria is proposed in this paper. And the method is used to develop some tuning formulae for the first-order plants with delay time. The comparison simulation experiments between the optimum neuron controller and the PID controllers are made. The results show that the optimum neuron control has better performances and stronger robustness.

articleTitle: One intelligent method for fault diagnosis and its application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: An intelligent method for fault diagnosis of a transformer is discussed based on chromatogram data, and a model of improved neural networks for fault synthesis diagnosis is presented. We have tested and verified the practical data of fault samples. Experiments prove that this method is practically variable, has a high recognition rate of faults and can be applied to the fault diagnosis of other electric equipment.

articleTitle: A zero-placement method to design robust time delay filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Proposes a technique for deriving extra insensitivity time delay filter using zero-placement in the discrete domain. Unlike previous derivations, this method leads to construction of a discrete transfer function to meet requirements on filter performance. This derivation is verified with the anti-sway control of cranes.

articleTitle: D-robust controller for multiple state delayed system with uncertain parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Satisfying control and estimation method is a new control and estimation idea. It meets as many satisfying indexes in engineering as possible, and does not attempt. It obtains controllers or estimators by general anti-solving Riccati equation. In this paper the sufficient condition for the existence of D-robust controller is presented for multiple state-delayed system with uncertain parameters. Considering the idea and the presented condition, the D-robust controller arithmetic is developed.

articleTitle: Robust tracking control using multiple models for uncertain systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on the positive and negative characteristics of the system output tracking error for the set-point input signal, the perturbations of the uncertain system with abrupt variation on a large scale within a working phase are divided into two classes. Each class can be stabilized robustly by an optimal robust tracking controller and the overall complex uncertain system can be controlled robustly on a large scale by the switching of the controllers. The idea and conclusion of the paper is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: An algorithm to reduce the number of simulation steps for optimizing closed Jackson network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: For optimizing the closed Jackson network, the gradient information obtained from perturbation analysis is a useful search method. However, in the simulation-based optimization, too many simulation steps is the major factor of reducing the optimization speed. We suggest a new method which uses the information derived from the simulation of old parameters to greatly enhance the speed of optimization.

articleTitle: Chaos algorithm of multilayer feedforward neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: By the use of the properties of ergodicity, a chaos algorithm for a multilayer feedforward neural network is proposed with combined logistic mapping and BP algorithm. This algorithm can make the BP algorithm skip the local minimum and can find the global minimum finally.

articleTitle: Dynamic non-idealities and their effect on the asymptotic behavior of discrete variable structure control systems with delays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, the exponential stability of the discrete linear singularly perturbed system with delay is studied by the space decomposition and systematic method. Based on the invariance criterion for the set /spl Omega//sub /spl alpha// of cone type and some structural transformations, some sufficient conditions have been formulated and small parameter estimates obtained that would guarantee the exponential stability of discrete variable structure systems (VSS) with delay and a discontinuous right-hand side. It is has been established, in particular, that the VSS with delay robust to regular perturbations are always robust to singular ones. The absolute stable robustness to dynamical nonidealities has been established for discrete time-invariant system with delay.

articleTitle: The composition and hierarchically structural model of car central intelligent control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The application of intelligent control technology to cars has become an important research direction. Based on the task of car central control and the research on the composition of a car central intelligent control system (CCICS), the paper presents and designs the structure of a car hierarchical central intelligent control system (CHCICS), which is guided by a hierarchical viewpoint of intelligent control strategy.

articleTitle: An efficient approach to reduce search space of capacity planning for PWB assembly system: random demand
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: An algorithm of determining the rough addition set for PWB assembly line capacity expansion problem under random demand is developed. For the single period problem, the algorithm can drop the size of integer decision variables dramatically and even to the extent that the corresponding problem can be directly solved by a standard integer programming code for realistic PWB assembly systems. The described algorithm can further help the heuristic search process or solving the procedure for the multiple-period problem.

articleTitle: Positive invariance of linear uncertain systems and applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Sufficient and necessary conditions for nonlinear impulsive systems with respect to linear constraints with bounded additive disturbances are obtained from a characterization of positive invariance properties for these systems. As an application of results obtained, the sufficient conditions for discrete state feedback control and for asymptotic stabilization of linear uncertain systems with the state positively nonsymmetrical invariant set are presented. Furthermore, extensions to multirate sampled-data control are presented. Finally, a numerical example is given.

articleTitle: Three-dimension fuzzy controller of novel design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: 3D fuzzy control is difficult to design. A new realization method is presented, for 3 stages of control. Its principles are given. Simulation results are given.

articleTitle: Using association rules to improve Chinese handwritten character recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Association rules are useful for determining correlation between attributes of a relation and have applications in marketing, financial and retail sectors. In this paper, we present an approach for combining handwritten character classifiers based on association rules, which reflect the correlation between the classifiers. The experimental results show that the association rules improve the performances of the integrated system significantly. An experimental comparison of two combination schemes is also provided.

articleTitle: A new method for linear model following adaptive control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper comes up with a new method for model following adaptive control. The key idea is to use linear controller, so as to avoid the problem of nonlinear infinite augmenting arithmetic operator in adaptive loops. Meanwhile, it has such virtues as simple calculation, short adaptive recycling, small following errors, etc. Using this method, we designed the sidelong control system of a fighter plane. The simulation on computer proves to be satisfactory.

articleTitle: A supervisory control system including digital simulation realized by PLC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper presents a thought of utilizing PLC to realize numeric simulation in complex control system. A example of simulation of disinfection process control system is introduced in detail to show the hardware and software structure of the supervisory control system.

articleTitle: Research on neural networks for compensated error of the gyro starting drift rate
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Using the results of some two degree of freedom gyroscope practical tests for neural network modeling, the starting drift rate model is employed for compensation of the gyro drift rate, and the effect of the neural network model for compensation of the gyro starting drift rate is deduced.

articleTitle: Adaptive backstepping control using neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive backstepping design method for a kind of affine nonlinear system with unknown nonlinearity and/or uncertainty. The neural network is used to approximate the unknown nonlinear function and/or uncertainty in the system. Then the neural adaptive backstepping controller without off-line training is obtained using conventional adaptive backstepping. According to the Lyapunov stability theory, the weight update law of neural network, the adaptive law of error bound, the stabilizing function and the control are obtained, thus the stability of closed-loop control system is ensured. The simulation result shows the effectiveness of adaptive backstepping control using neural networks.

articleTitle: Nonlinear electro-mechanical coupled oscillation and control for power electronic converter drives
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: With power electronic converter drives for a research object, the oscillation or vibration phenomena occurring in practical applications are analyzed in the paper. For the nonlinear-coupled oscillation, the mechanism and the control method are studied. A control strategy is proposed the paper. The control strategy is used to suppress hoist mechanical vibration and shaft winding-tower vibration. The effects of vibration or oscillation control are remarkable. It provides an available theoretical method to solve the problems of oscillation or vibration occurring in practical engineering.

articleTitle: The Lyapunov stability analysis on restraint loops of a two-degree-of-freedom gyro
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The stability of the restraint loops of a two degree-of-freedom (DOF) gyro has been analyzed by means of the Lyapunov direct method. The state-space model is derived from the technical functions of a 2-DOF gyro, which is a fourth-order system and time varying during the starting process. From the variable gradient method, the Lyapunov function is found, and whereby the stability conditions of the system are obtained. Since the starting process of a gyro is much longer than the time constant of the restraint loops for time-varying systems, it can be stabilized as long as the stability conditions are changed along with the time varying parameters.

articleTitle: Nonlinear adaptive pattern recognition of matter-element analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Using the nonlinear mapping method, this paper maps the multidimensional nonlinear data onto the low-dimension space to improve the linear degree, and then incorporates the adaptive pattern recognition of matter-element analysis to sort data. We also present the group pattern recognition method of nonlinear adaptive matter-element analysis.

articleTitle: Study on fractal model for radar clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The fractal property of the clutter series is studied briefly by means of the power spectrum, correlation function and scalar dual logarithm relationship analyses. The time-variant surface is proposed to describe the local dynamic characteristics of the scattered surface, and the time-domain fractal property of the scattered field from an actual surface is analysed qualitatively with Kirchhoff's solution under three rational assumptions on electromagnetic scattering. Finally, the random fractal model for the clutter is deduced, and the amplitude distribution, power spectrum and parameter property are discussed in brief. Both the theoretical deduction and the analysis on real-life data demonstrate that the clutter approximates random fractal signals, and the random fractal model is valid for the clutter modeling.

articleTitle: Synthesis signal process of digital sonar system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper introduces the structure and performance of the ADSP-2106X DSP briefly, and then the synthesis process design of digital sonar system is discussed in detail, which include the measurement of target's distance, speed and orientation, to complete the target's search and judgement. Based on the result, algorithm model and realization of multiple mobile target track is improved. Compare with the result of the system test, we can conclude that the synthesis process design can satisfy the designer's need.

articleTitle: An equivalent sample circuit based on DSP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper introduces an equivalent sample circuit based on DSP. With the technology of equivalent sample, this circuit can sample signal of maximum 10 GSPS equivalent sample rate under the condition of 40 MSPS single-shot real sample rate. This paper describes the design theory and its advantage.

articleTitle: Man-machine intelligent working systems for grinding robots
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Man-machine intelligent working system (MMIWS) is a kind of system that inter-fuses human intelligent and machine intelligent with the addition of working ability, and can deal with the indeterminate operation tasks in the non-structured environment. One example of this is the partial grinding robot that can be used in iron and steel plants. There are scars and blemishes on the steel ingots or billets after rolling which must be cleared away by grinding. These tasks of operation can not determined in advance because scars or blemishes on the surface of each billet to be grinding vary in distribution, shape, size, depth and quantity. In the man-machine intelligent working systems, the human intelligence can entered into the system at every levels such as the task plan level, path program level, motion control level and so on, so that both the human and machine intelligences can be combined nicely.

articleTitle: Predictive PI control based on fuzzy model for time-delay systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Presents a kind of predictive PI controller based on a fuzzy model for large time-delay systems. The controller adopts the control strategy of generalized predictive control (GPC). The control algorithm is simple and easy to implement. The fuzzy model and parameters of the controller are corrected using a steepest descent algorithm. The simulation result shows its better performance than conventional PID controller for plants with large time-delay.

articleTitle: Asymptotic pole assignment by learning
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper solves the exact pole assignment problem for the single-input stochastic systems with unknown coefficients under the controllability assumption which is necessary and sufficient for the arbitrary pole assignment for systems with known coefficients. The system noise is required to be mutually independent with zero mean and bounded second moment, and the state at a fixed time is assumed to be repeatedly observable for different feedback gains. This paper applies the iterative learning approach which is essentially based on stochastic approximation. The feedback gains are given without invoking the certainty-equivalency principle.

articleTitle: The distributed measurement and control system of heat treatment factory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Describes the system which utilizes 4C technology (computer technology, automatic control technology, communication technology and CRT technology) to: monitor, control and administrate the heat treatment factory's production process; implement the heat treatment technology's automation and integrated control and administration; and improve the production efficiency, saving many manpower resources, ensuring the product's quality and stability and bringing economical effective and social benefit to the factory.

articleTitle: Industrial distillation column advanced control in a DCS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Some aspects of using DCS to implement propylene/propane splitter advanced control are considered, including enthalpic control of column reboiler, multivariable control of top product quality and bottom product quality, fuzzy supervisory control of process load, etc. Industrial application results show that advanced control can increase the splitter tower stability, improve the distillate product quality and increase recovery of distillate product while reducing energy consumption.

articleTitle: A tunable QoS routing algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: We propose a new distributed route-selection scheme to look for a feasible route satisfying the quality of service (QoS) constraints without compromising any of the existing guarantees. The performance of the QoS routing algorithm is tunable by choosing different upper bounds of the expected delivery time at every node according to the status of the network. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed route-selection scheme.

articleTitle: Adaptive quasi-sliding mode control for discrete nonlinear system with uncertain model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The problem of adaptive quasi-sliding mode control for a class of discrete nonlinear systems with uncertain model is studied in this paper. Based on the principle of sliding mode control and the approximation capability of neural networks, an adaptive-NN-based model is built, and a synthetical design scheme of adaptive quasi-sliding mode controller is proposed. In order to achieve robust performance against system's parameter variations and external disturbances, or reduce tracking errors, an adaptive control law is given. Both the NN rights and the controller parameters are regulated adaptively online. The simulation results show that the closed-loop adaptive quasi-sliding mode control system is stable, with tracking errors converging to a neighborhood of zero.

articleTitle: An algorithm for the mixed /spl mu/ synthesis in the state-space
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on the interior-point method, a state-space algorithm for mixed /spl mu/ synthesis is proposed. Then the algorithm is illustrated by computer simulation. Besides robust stability, the system designed by the presented method has short regulating period and small overshoot.

articleTitle: Application of inductance matrix in digital simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Due to the fact that the inductance matrix of a three-phase induction motor is a cycle one and characteristics of the cycle matrix combinations are valid, it is preferable to derive the correlative expressions between the inductance matrix and its inverse, and the result can then be obtained simply by assignment instead of calling subroutines in order to reduce the computation time. The computation time required by this approach is compared with that by coordinate transformation.

articleTitle: The state space model and stability analysis of a neuron control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A state space model of a neuron control system is proposed and the stability analysis of the system is presented. For typical industrial plants, the relationship between controller parameters and system stability is studied. The method and results are helpful for understanding the mechanism of the neuron controller and its design for industrial applications.

articleTitle: The production-inventory model with time-dependent demand and time-limited free back-orders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Studies a production-inventory model with time-limited free back-orders by assuming time-dependent demand and finite replenishment rate. An efficient iterative procedure is proposed to provide the optimal production and inventory schedule with the help of a computer. Models with linear trend in demand are analyzed as special cases. Numerical examples are included to illustrate the proposed solution procedure. The results of these examples provide theoretical evidence for the inventory system to make management decisions.

articleTitle: Orbit acquisition and trajectory rendezvous control of CBERS-1
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The CBERS-1 is the first Sun-synchronous orbit resource satellite cooperatively developed by China and Brazil. The CBERS-1 had been successfully launched into the designed orbit by the Chinese Long-March launch vehicle. It has been normally operated in the high-accuracy Sun-synchronous, recursive, frozen orbit designed for remote-sensing users through a series of orbit acquisition, sub-satellite-point trace acquisition and orbit maintenance manoeuvres. The paper briefly presents the mission objectives, system structure, orbit control strategy, control performance, flight software and on-orbit operations for the orbit control system of the CBERS-1, as well as its flight results.

articleTitle: Adaptive stabilization of unstable periodic orbits of chaotic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: An adaptive time-delayed control method is proposed for stabilizing inherent unstable periodic orbits (UPOs) in chaotic systems. We first formulate the UPO stabilizing problem as a nonlinear optimal control problem, the analytic solution to which results in a controller stabilizing the desired UPOs. We then use the synchronization concept to construct an identifier for the estimation of the uncertain system parameters. We prove that under the developed scheme, the system parameter estimates will converge to their true values.

articleTitle: Inverse of a sampled system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: We study the invertibility of a sampled data system. Necessary and sufficient invertibility conditions are given explicitly in terms of transfer function zeros. It is shown that many systems including those with "unstable" zeros or those with more inputs than outputs are in fact stably invertible. Detailed design procedures to achieve the system inverse are given. A minimum sensitivity inverse with respect to under-modeling and noise is also provided in the paper.

articleTitle: Double-advantage controller of novel design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: To solve the control problem of an object with non-linear characteristics, ambiguity and disturbance etc., a double-advantage controller of novel design which has fast input tracking and excellent disturbance rejection is stated. Its design thoughts and realization are introduced in detail. The result of simulation tests show the double-advantage controller of novel design has excellent effect.

articleTitle: On the minimal-order of dynamic output regulators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The minimal-order problem of the dynamic output regulators of linear time-invariant systems is considered, and a lower bound for the minimal-order is given. Unlike in previous works, the lower bound presented is a simple function of the system dimension and ranks of the input and output matrices, computation involves neither a rank minimization problem nor a semi-definite programming problem. An example is given to illustrate the non-conservativeness of the lower bound.

articleTitle: A practical evolutionary algorithm of one dimensional stock cutting problem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on the characteristic of one dimensional stock cutting problem, combined the linear programming and the evolutionary computation, an approximation algorithm for the problem is given, which is easy and fast in implementation. Experiment shows that the using rate of material is up to 97.5% in average and the algorithm is worth of practice.

articleTitle: The design methods of current-mode nth-order filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The design methods of nth-order filters by means of current conveyor (CC) are studied, the filter circuits using second-generation CC and multi-output CC (MOCC) are compared, and the merit and defect of two design methods are analyzed. The result states clearly that an nth-order filter designed by means of MOCC has a small mount component and simple structure and has good potential for use in information processing.

articleTitle: The application of neural networks for the army oil supply
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This article adopts two developed methods-Hopfield networks (HN) and self-organization networks (SONN)-to find the most appropriate supply-center for the army to use for the supply of petroleum. 2 methods are discussed and are compared with the traditional optimum technique.

articleTitle: CMAC neural networks-based adaptive control for discrete-time nonlinear systems with unmatched uncertainties by backstepping
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Considers adaptive control for a class of SISO discrete-time nonlinear systems with unmatched uncertainties. The discrete-time nonlinear systems with unmatched uncertainties are firstly transformed into a class of new discrete-time nonlinear systems with matched uncertainties, and a CMAC neural network-based controller which linearizes the new discrete-time nonlinear systems is presented. Secondly, the states of the new discrete-time nonlinear systems are estimated using CMAC neural networks by backstepping. A stability proof is given in the sense of Lyapunov using the persistency of excitation (PE) condition. It is shown that all the signals in the closed-loop system are uniformly ultimately bounded. A simulation example is also given.

articleTitle: Researches on the network support environment of the collaboration-based virtual laboratory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: With the development of the broadband IP platform, the Internet-based collaboration applications not only improve efficiency, but also save money. The paper investigates the network support environment of the virtual laboratory, including the gateway queue mechanism and end-to-end congestion mechanism. Then we analyze the shortcomings of the current mechanisms, and present an adaptive end-to-end congestion mechanism based on the UDP which guarantees minimum rates. Finally, we briefly evaluate our method and discuss how to improve it.

articleTitle: Parameter tracking for stochastic time-varying systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Describes a method for tracking fast time-varying parameters of dynamic systems under stochastic disturbances. Auxiliary information is used in addition to the plant input and output for better tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: A kind of "growing" function link nets and its application in the prediction of oil field yield
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A kind of new "growing" functional link nets prediction models and recursive Gauss-Newton learning algorithm are stated. These new networks and learning algorithm have the characteristics of fast learning and training speed and high prediction precision. They have been successfully applied to prediction problems of oil field yield. Validity of the new scheme is indicated.

articleTitle: Statistical process monitoring with measured data corrupted by noise and gross error
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is an efficient method to extract relationships between correlated variables and thus has been widely applied to the multivariate statistical process monitoring. However, the validity of the PCA is highly depending on the quality of measured process data which is usually contaminated by noises and gross errors in practice. In this paper, an improved PCA is presented to minimize the influences of corrupted data. The original measured data is first processed using conventional PCA to partially eliminate noises by abandoning principal components with small eigenvalues. Then the retained principal components are decomposed and rectified online by boundary-corrected wavelets, combined with techniques of shift-invariant transform and median filtering. The monitoring results of a simulated binary distillation column show that the proposed method has superior performance and more robust to noises and gross errors than conventional methods.

articleTitle: Intelligent control and adaptation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)

articleTitle: An adaptive fuzzy combinatorial neural network model for predicting the composition of Pb-Zn agglomerate
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Considering the characteristics of neural network modeling and empirical mechanism modeling, an adaptive fuzzy combinatorial model structure is proposed to effectively combine the two modeling methods together by use of the fuzzy classification. In the paper, the adaptive fuzzy combinatorial modeling is applied to the prediction of Pb-Zn agglomerate composition. Simulation results show that the proposed modeling is effective in the prediction of composition and meets the requirement of optimization computation for the blending process.

articleTitle: An intelligent gradient method and its application to parameter identification of dynamical linear processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: An intelligent gradient method is proposed for optimization problems in dynamical environments. This is an extension to the work of Zhou et al. (1993). According to a measure of dynamical performances, intelligent strategies determine recursive actions which improves dynamical performances. The proposed method is directly applied to parameter identification of dynamical linear systems in the form of intelligent recursive least squares (IRLS) algorithm. Related simulations are performed to investigate some of the properties, e.g., convergence and robustness. A significant saving in the computational cost can be achieved by the IRLS algorithm with almost no sacrifice of the estimation accuracy and of the parameter tracking ability.

articleTitle: A kind of optimizing parameter method for vector control AC drive system used right-across experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, a kind of optimizing parameter method for vector control AC drive system is presented. This method optimizes parameters of the system by experiment, eliminating parameter errors in theoretical calculation and accumulative parameter errors resulting from unit errors. The experiment result indicates that the method is accurate for parameter recognition, simple to operate and easy to realize.

articleTitle: Sift algorithm to improve performance of Chinese character classifier using linear decision function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Presents a method to improve the performance of a Chinese character classifier. The method examines the candidates of an existing classifier using a linear decision function to select the most probable one. The algorithm together with a complete scheme has been proposed. The possible improvement of the performance has been estimated based on the experimental inspection of the separability of Chinese characters. The result shows that recognition accuracy can be increased dramatically. This means that the algorithm is practical.

articleTitle: Data processing of roll-shape measurement system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, data processing methods of roll-shape measurement system are discussed. We separately use least square method and neural network method to fit the curve of roll-shape. The results show that fitting precision of the neural network method is better than that of least-squares method.

articleTitle: The research of control method in aluminum electrolysis computer control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: According to the problems existing in aluminum electrolysis control system at present, this paper presents a feed forward PID controller with two free degree. The controller has satisfying tracing and noise-preventing features, which cause the electrolysis to work optimally and thus increase the current efficiency, decrease energy consumption, and improve the control effect to a great extent. This has great significance in improving the quality and quantity of aluminum.

articleTitle: Three layer architecture model in network manufacturing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: According to the features of network manufacturing, the three-layer structure model of C/S based on middle layer was put forward. The topic analyses the evaluation criterion and implement processes of middle layer in detail, which is the core technology of network manufacturing. This three-layer structure establishes the basement for standard and openness of network topology architecture on network manufacturing.

articleTitle: ANN-driven fuzzy reasoning model of product green attributes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: According to expert judgement, the main influencing factors on product green attributes are obtained by the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) in the paper. An ANN-driven fuzzy reasoning model of product green attributes is developed. The results of the relation between product green attributes and its influencing factors obtained from experts are used as sample set and the ANN can be trained by the sample set. The expert's idea can been refined from the model by the trained system so as to use it to assess product green attributes. An example is given in the paper and a good result is achieved in material attribute assessment.

articleTitle: Study of low altitude flight trajectory control of aircraft
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The hierarchical control theory of related large-scale systems is used to study the trajectory tracking problem of six degree-of-freedom aircraft which have vertical and horizontal orientation coupling. A good control result is obtained via the partial control laws design independently of the vertical and horizontal orientation, and the global control laws design in which coupling factors are taken into consideration. The method presented avoids the conventional decoupling process, reduces the difficulty of theoretical study and is easy to realize in engineering.

articleTitle: The research on the international propagation mechanism of financial volatility based on the global large-scale system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper firstly points out that along with the rapid progress of global economic-financial integration, the country economic systems have been evolving into a world economic large-scale system with strong coupling among the subsystems from the initial isolated disperse systems. Therefore the international propagation of financial volatility should be researched from the point of view of the global large-scale system. The economic-financial link model of three countries is established. The economic system, which the model describes, is a double time-scale system. With an eye to the feedback structure in the system, the effects of several link channels among which the financial one is the leading one in the origin, propagation, eruption and stabilization of the financial crises are analyzed. Finally the analysis of the model shows that the fragility of the financial system in the age of the global integration is rooted in the fundamental changes happening to the link structure among the subsystems of the world economic large-scale system, and the financial link mechanism has been critical to the structural changes.

articleTitle: About solution of the continuous-time algebraic Riccati equation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The algorithm for the construction of a stabilising solution of algebraic Riccati equation (ARE) is considered. This algorithm is required for the determination of the special solution of quadratic matrix equation. It is shown that the solution searched for this equation can be expressed through the sign function of an appropriate matrix. It is noted that the basic relation of the algorithm is based on the known relations of the matrix sign function method.

articleTitle: The method of design for MLPNN's structure based on species evolutionary GA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In dealing with the design of neural network's structure and drawbacks of the normal design methods, this paper proposes a new method for designing the multilayer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) structure based on species evolutionary genetic algorithms. This method of combining the neural network (NN) and genetic algorithm (GA) has the superiority of NN's structure training speed and fitness. The simulation and application demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A two-sector economy evolution model based on the general equilibrium and its simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A macro-economic system is divided into a new and developing sector and a traditional or developed sector in the paper, a nonlinear two-sector economic system evolution model is set up. Under general equilibrium, the evolution process of this economic system is discussed, and the solution is given. It is proven to be unstable by model analysis and simulation, and a bifurcation appears in the economic variable growth path. The mid-trajectory of this bifurcation is the turnpike of the nonlinear two-sector economic system evolution process.

articleTitle: A novel parallel multiobjective genetic algorithm and its application in process scheduling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper proposes a parallel multiobjective genetic algorithm to solve process scheduling problems with the characteristics of multiobjectives, hybrid dynamics and real time computation. An objective ranking evaluation technique is developed to associate the trade-off information to a better solution with preference articulation. A novel double-layer chromosome coding method is used to express the system hybridness. Computation time is at least reduced to 10 percent of its original value by adopting a hierarchical decomposed parallel computing technique. Simulation results show that the algorithm illustrated has prospective applications to complex process scheduling optimization problems.

articleTitle: Two degree optimal steady tracking controller design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper addresses the robust steady tracking problem when the system under consideration is subjected to norm bounded time-varying uncertainty, and the reference input signal and the external disturbance under consideration are the signal set with known dynamic characteristic polynomials. The controller design procedure is partitioned into deadbeat control design for nominal system and optimal steady-tracking control design, by using two-degree control scheme and Youla parametrization. With the deadbeat controller set and the exact formulas for computing robust steady performance measure presented by Khammash (1995), the optimal steady tracking design problem is converted into a finite dimensional l/sub 1/ optimization. The design method presented is simple and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Optimal solution and approximate solutions of SISO mixed H/sub 2//l/sub 1/ problem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The SISO mixed H/sub 2//l/sub 1/ problem for discrete time systems is studied. It is shown that there exists a unique optimal solution for this problem. The optimal solution can be approximated within any prescribed missing error bound in l/sub 2/ norm with solvable suboptimal solutions and solvable super-optimal solutions.

articleTitle: Self-organizing fuzzy controller for synchronization of two motor axes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A general method is developed to generate fuzzy control rules by self-organizing and self-learning. This method includes 3 steps: step 1 establishes the experimental system to obtain the data or describing the dynamic characteristics of the system to be considered at real time; step 2 combines the numerical information into a fuzzy rule base to describe the dynamic characteristics of the system, which emulates the operators or domain experts to obtain the linguistic representations of the system; and step 3 uses the dynamic characteristics obtained to design the fuzzy controller by the complex optimization method. The experimental results demonstrate the high performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: The design of robust adaptive controller applied in automobile active suspension
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This article proposes a new robust adaptive control algorithm from applied point of view which can be applied to active suspension. Its stability is proved and simulated in disturbed system. Firstly, a nonlinear filter is introduced. It simplifies the control law design. Secondly, the analysis of VSC (variable structure control) is used in backstepping controller design. The robustness to system disturbance is gained.

articleTitle: Intelligent agent-based IN service creation environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper presents the intelligent agent-based network (IN) service creation environment (ISCE) to create automatically new service by means of intelligent agent technology. This paper introduces the intelligent agent concept to IN architecture and proposes IA-based IN architecture. Based on the proposed architecture, the intelligent service creation environment is implemented. The ISCE can distribute effectively the intelligence between intelligent services and service creation managers, reduce the complexity and improve the ability of the service creation of IN.

articleTitle: The stair-like generalized predictive control for main-steam pressure of boiler in steam-power plant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper analyses the dynamic behavior of main-steam pressure of boiler in steam-power plant, uses generalized predictive control for main-steam pressure, describes a modified generalized predictive control algorithm which becomes more robust and has strong anti-disturbance ability for application of stair-like control scheme, implements the main-steam pressure control and gets good control performance.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of trajectory tracing control of 6-DOF parallel manipulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Based on the dynamic model of 6-DOF parallel manipulators, a method used to investigate the stability of control strategies for trajectory tracing is proposed under a uniform frame. Using this method, the stability and the stable area of a classical control strategy, PD plus estimated nominal input, is discussed. And the method developed in this paper also has general use to other kinds of control strategies, so we can obtain their stability and the stable area in the same way. Simulation verified that the results which we had got using this control strategy had the same stability as we had analyzed.

articleTitle: Tracking object using improved Hausdorff measure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper describes the techniques for tracking nonrigid object moving in a complex scene. The improvement incorporates that both location and orientation information are used in model-matching and model-updating process. In this paper, we also propose a highly efficient searching strategy of locating object in an image. Results indicate that these techniques can perform well in complex conditions such as moving background and moving camera.

articleTitle: Observer-based robust H/sub /spl infin// control for uncertain time delay systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of observer-based H/sub /spl infin// control for uncertain time-delay systems. Based on the observer states, a controller is proposed to stabilizing the systems, and it can also guarantee that the H/sub /spl infin// norm from the disturbance to the output is bounded. The controller can be obtained by solving two algebraic Riccati equations.

articleTitle: Optimal structure of FWL digital controller with pole sensitivity minimization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper studies the optimal realizations of a finite-word-length (FWL) digital state-estimate feedback controller with closed-loop pole sensitivity minimization considerations. Through analysis it is shown that the pole sensitivity measure is coordinate dependent. Structures that minimize this measure are found.

articleTitle: Estimation-based recursive algorithm for the identification of a discontinuous output sampling system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: System identification is usually based on continuous sampling presumption, but discontinuous sampling may happen in some real applications. Each sample value is to be used by some of the equations. Without the equations due to discontinuation, the total number of usable equations will reduce significantly, and the identification calculation will become less efficient. When the rate of lost sample increases to a criticality value, there is no equation left to do the traditional identification calculation. A new estimation-based recursive algorithm is suggested. In the algorithm the estimated output sample values are used instead of the lost ones, and appropriate equations are established, so that the efficiency will not decrease too much by the discontinuation of sample. By means of the appropriate equations, the calculation can be done even when the critical lost rate is reached. The analysis shows that the algorithm converges with probability in the vicinity of the real value. Simulation shows that it is efficient and practical.

articleTitle: An optimal strategy for parallel processing of speech signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Studies parallel processing algorithms of linear prediction of speech parameters. The autoregressive speech vector series with stable covariance, can be gained after a classification of adjacent samples of source speech series. A strategy of vector predictive coding with highly parallel processing ability can be achieved with the application of the principle of orthogonal projection in Hilbert space. Finally it is confirmed that the algorithms are effective by computer simulation.

articleTitle: The application of neural network and evolutionary algorithm in mechanical optimal design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Discusses the application of several neural network models and evolutionary algorithm in mechanical optimal design. A time-varying recurrent neural network model, Hopfield model, BP model, Boltzmann model, Gauss model, evolution neural network model and evolutionary algorithm and their applications in mechanical optimal design are discussed also.

articleTitle: Agent brigade in dynamic formation of robotic soccer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper a new architecture of multi-agent in robotic soccer is introduced. It adopts the agent brigade approach in dynamic formation of robotic soccer. By dividing the soccer field into three areas according to the roles of agents, this approach can dynamically switch the roles of agents in each area temporarily to achieve local predominance that may lend to initiative in the match.

articleTitle: Analysing epileptic events online by neural nets, special preprocessing methods included
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Normally EEG-signatures are analysed in the frequency domain while a common FFT- or wavelet-transformation transforms the time signals of the electromagnetic activities of the (wet) neurons into the frequency domain. We show that better and faster results can be obtained if instead of these common algorithms the FD-operation is applied to the pure time-signal and a difference-autopower-spectrum (DAS) calculation for eliminating the noisy contributions is done next. Especially we compare the signatures of some epilepsy events analysed by common signal analysis and by the class-oriented DAS- and FD-operations and discuss the results.

articleTitle: Solving nonstandard job-shop scheduling problem with due dates using bounding genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: According to the features of a non-standard job-shop scheduling problem with due dates, using the reverse scheduling policy, a initial algorithm based on priority values is presented in this paper, and the operators of the bounding genetic algorithm are constructed. Demonstration and judgement of the deadlock are also proposed. The experiment result shows that the algorithm presented is effective and can converge faster.

articleTitle: Studying and accomplishing a new guidance law for homing missile attacking maneuvering target
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: By utilizing the design method of the linear-quadratic regulator, a new optimal guidance law for the infrared and radar homing missile which has good adaptability and high precision for attacking maneuvering target is derived. For resolving the important problem in engineering accomplishing, an adaptive statistical model of target maneuvering is proposed. Based on the statistical model of target maneuvering and nonlinear Kalman filter, a new algorithm which uses infrared AGC signal or radar range measure signal to estimate maneuvering targets acceleration distance and velocity between missile and target is proposed. The simulation of two missile control and guide systems prove that the algorithm has good stability and convergence.

articleTitle: Fuzzy synthesize neural networks and application to distinguish flying action
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Mechanics of neural networks and fuzzy logic are analyzed in the paper, and the fusion of neural network systems and fuzzy logic systems is analyzed too. We propose a model based on the fuzzy synthesize function and show complete adaptive learning algorithms at the same time. The fuzzy synthesize mapping networks were used, and we obtained a highly accurate rate of identification.

articleTitle: Nonexistence of positives solutions of a class nonlinear delay discrete dynamic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Necessary conditions are derived for the existence of positive solutions of a class of nonlinear delay discrete dynamic systems. The technique used to derive these conditions is based on the nonexistence of positive roots of an associated characteristic equation.

articleTitle: Indirect adaptive fuzzy control of discrete-time nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, an indirect adaptive controller based on fuzzy logic systems is shown to provide the tracking of a reference signal for a class of discrete-time nonlinear systems. The fuzzy logic system is used as the system model of the plant dynamics that are unknown, and the adaptive controller is then constructed based on the model. Assuming the modelling error is bounded, it is proved that the resulting closed-loop control system is globally stable in the sense that both the input and output signals are uniformly bounded, and the tracking error is within a limited band. Simulation examples are given.

articleTitle: Approximation capability of fuzzy input-output systems based on similarity measures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Fuzzy input-output systems based upon similarity measures are proposed. It is shown that the proposed fuzzy systems can approximate, to any degree of accuracy, a continuous fuzzy function. Approximation mechanisms of fuzzy systems based upon the distances of fuzzy sets are explicitly exploited.

articleTitle: The simulation analysis in the speed sensorless DC servo system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The sensor for detecting the feedback value of current and speed is needed in a double closed DC servo system. A two dimensional observer that can estimate the value of speed and load torque is designed. Using the state observer theory, an estimated value is used in the DC servo system, and the load torque achieves interference compensation. The simulation results achieved the designed requirements.

articleTitle: A explicit rate calculating flow control of ATM networking
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper compares several kinds of flow control schemes, and analyzes their advantages and disadvantages. On the basis of the rate based flow control algorithm, the explicit rate calculating algorithm with max-min fairness, a new rate based flow control scheme with perfect fairness, high channel utilization and satisfaction for the virtual channel requests, is proposed.

articleTitle: R&D on translation technique in enterprise information publishing management system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: This paper discusses the solution to mono-language problem of enterprise information publishing and management systems (EIPMS) based on the Web technique, which meaning that most of the information publishing and management systems in China can only provide Chinese information and can not use the worldwide popular codes. A translation technique, the multidimension translation technology (MDTT), is one of the key technologies to this problem. Under the research and development of a large information publishing and management system, such as EIPMS, this paper presents the details of MDTT.

articleTitle: An intelligent ladle furnace control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper, an intelligent ladle furnace control system is presented. The main functions and system structure is introduced. The system applied combined artificial intelligent technology for ladle furnace heat balance calculation and steel temperature prediction, dynamic energy input optimization and intelligent electrode control. The application results achieved are given to demonstrate the capability or this intelligent control system.

articleTitle: Application of knowledge-based systems in multisensor data fusion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: With the progress of related development tools and methods, the knowledge-based system is applied broadly in multisensor data fusion problems especially in situation assessment (SA) and threat assessment (TA) domain. This paper discusses in detail a particularly implemented architecture of knowledge-based system (KBS), the blackboard architecture. The blackboard architecture provides a method to model the way a group of experts would attempt to solve the SA or TA problems cooperatively through the communication among multiple knowledge sources. This paper also analyses its advantages and disadvantages, and one practical example is presented.

articleTitle: Implementation of a 12.8 kbit/s LD-CELP speech codec
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The paper presents a 12.8 kbit/s LD-CELP speech coding algorithm that is based on the G.728 speech coding standard. The method can decrease effectively the size of the vector quantization codebook by doing a statistical experiment on the codeword use frequency for the codebook. The results show that the algorithm can hold better synthesised speech quality than other same type ways. Finally, the algorithm is implemented in duplex real-time on a high speed DSP system with two TMS320C31s.

articleTitle: An approach to fault diagnosis of industrial cracking furnaces via neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: In this paper,an approach to fault diagnosis of industrial cracking furnaces is presented by using functional-link neural networks and the fast recursive learning algorithm. This technique considerably integrates neural networks and expert systems, and makes it possible to simultaneously diagnose multiple faults and their corresponding levels in the cracking process. A simulation study shows successful results for the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Inclusion principle of dual systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The dual inclusion is defined for the dual system in this paper. The dual relationship of the inclusion conditions between the original system and the dual system is given. The restriction condition of dual systems is the compensation for the aggregation condition of original systems.

articleTitle: Multivariable intelligent decoupling control and its applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)

articleTitle: A kind of new self-tuning filter and its application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The CARMA model of the systems are developed by system identification methods and its parameters are estimated. Moreover, the state space models of the systems are given according to the lemma of time sequence models and state space models. A new self-tuning filter is described. It comprises the recursive extended least square estimator, Kalman filter and noise statistical estimator. Applied to oil field systems, excellent results were obtained. Validity of the new scheme is indicated.

articleTitle: The predictive functional control algorithm of bilinear system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Richalet (1987) presented the predictive functional control (PFC) method which is based on the basic predictive control principle. PFC has the following advantages: a simple algorithm, less calculation on line and high control precision. It has been applied to many different control areas successfully, but few results on the PFC algorithm for nonlinear systems have been reported. In this paper, a new nonlinear predictive functional control (NPFC) algorithm is presented and the obtained NPFC algorithm can be applied to bilinear system with disturbance. The simulation results show that the NPFC control strategy is quite effective and has the following advantages: disturbance attenuation, good tracking performance and high control precision.

articleTitle: The recognition and analysis system of blood cells
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The research on recognition and diagnosis of blood cells in medicine has great value. A trisection blood cell, quintuple leucocyte, checking and collection of abnormal cells can be realized by the recognition and analysis system of blood cells which is mainly composed of a color CCD, a picture grab card and a PC etc. The system can be used to deal with many kinds of cells of the human body.

articleTitle: A research on ultrasonic level measuring system for tank
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: The ultrasonic level measurement technology is a technique developed for a tank gauge, but due to its complexity is limited in application. In view of the characteristics of the tank gauge, a new measuring approach is presented and an ultrasonic level measuring system is developed, the tests are also described. Through analyzing the test data, some conclusions are reached: the ultrasonic level measuring has high reliability, good stability and is intrinsically safe, but has shortcomings of poor accuracy and low resolution.

articleTitle: Research and implementation of fieldbus reliability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: Flexibility of constructing redundant control system is one of the main features of Foundation Fieldbus (FF). Based on the protocol of FF, levels of component redundancy are discussed in detail, and an instance of an FF based control system with redundancy is analyzed. The analysis indicates that FF is flexible for configuring a redundant system which plays an important role in completely improving the reliability of a control system.

articleTitle: Nonlinear neural predictive control with control constraints
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A neural model is applied to predictive control and a neural model constrained predictive control (NMCPC) algorithm for a nonlinear process is proposed. In this algorithm, the neural model and nonlinear programming by gradient optimization are combined to obtain the optimal control law. The simulation result shows that NMCPC could achieve satisfactory control performance.

articleTitle: Neural network adaptive control with fuzzy rules confirming initial weights
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 3rd World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (Cat. No.00EX393)
abstract: A method, based on fuzzy rules, is presented to learn the initial values of a neural network's weight array. This neural network is used in an adaptive control architecture. Using the prior knowledge efficiently, it can ensure the stability of the adaptive control during the learning period of the neural network. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: Optimal integrated bidding and hydrothermal scheduling with risk management and self-scheduling requirements
